title: Laken Riley Act

claims.claim: requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain any non-citizen (mandatory)
claims.sourceSpan: shall effectively and expeditiously take
claims.note: Amends 236(c) (the INA mandatory-detention provision) and the new (3) commands "shall issue a detainer ... shall effectively and expeditiously take custody" — mandatory ("shall"), not discretionary. DHS = "Secretary of Homeland Security."

claims.claim: who entered the country unlawfully or without required documents

The gloss "entered unlawfully or without required documents" describes INA 212(a)(6)(A)/(7), which is not in the fetched source (no referencedSource for 212(a)), and it drops the (6)(C) fraud/misrepresentation ground. Not contradicted; standard statutory reading, but extrinsic.

claims.claim: [omission] Section 236(e) amended: strikes "or release" and "grant, revocation, or denial" -> "revocation or denial", narrowing the no-judicial-review bar so release/bond/parole decisions become reviewable (predicate for the new 236(f) state-AG suits) — not mentioned in the analysis
claims.sourceSpan: by striking ``or release
claims.note: Section 3(b)(1) amends 236(e): "by striking ``or release''" and "``grant, revocation, or denial'' and insert ``revocation or denial''." This removes release/grant decisions from the 1226(e) no-review shield — the enabling mechanism for the 236(f) suits. The suit effect is captured (top_lines "release decisions"), but the 236(e) change itself is unmentioned. Technical; effect surfaced elsewhere.

notes: Enacted amendatory bill (Public Law 119-1), full source read (enrolled/public-law text, 8342 chars). Analysis is faithful. No material issues. Non-SUPPORTED/caveated rows are all minor: (a) extrinsic statutory glosses of INA grounds not fetched — 212(a)(6)(A)/(6)(C)/(7) "entered unlawfully/fraud/no documents", 243(d) "countries that refuse to accept deportees", 1252(f)(1) "class-wide" injunction bar (accurate as law but unsourced within the hostile scope); (b) 1 breadth-of-support framing ("bipartisan support"); (c) 2 CR floor quotes unverifiable against bill source (no referencedSources); (d) defendant-list incompleteness ("DHS or the Attorney General" omits the Secretary of State for the 243(e) visa category); (e) 3 omissions (236(e) judicial-review-bar change, 212(d)(5) AG->DHS parole-authority transfer, and 236(f) release/bond/parole category dropped from the sections detail five-category list though present in top_lines). Figures ($100, dates, PL 119-1) and directions (expand/carve-out/mandatory) all verified against source; vote counts (64-35, 263-156) cross-checked against votes[].
